findings.message: The Hindi sentence ends with one verb pair for both objects: 'हमारे मन का आनन्द, जो दिन-रात प्रसन्न रखे, और परम श्री का सर्वोच्च पद बढ़ाए और प्रदान करे।' Read naturally, both verbs then govern both objects, which gives the odd phrase 'पद बढ़ाए'. The English keeps the two verbs apart ('spread ... joy ... and grant ... seat'). The meaning can still be worked out, so this is a matter of natural style rather than a clear error. A human should decide.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the w5 segment so each verb follows its own object, as the English already does by using w5 three times. Line 3: add {refs:[w5], text:'बढ़ाए,'} after the w8 segment and change that segment to 'जो दिन-रात प्रसन्न रखे,'. Line 4: 'और परम श्री का' (w9) / 'सर्वोच्च' (w10) / 'पद' (w11) / {refs:[w5], text:'प्रदान करे।'}.
